title: Automated individual decisions: basis, information and human intervention
summary: What a controller records to show, for a decision based solely on automated processing, which exception it relied on, what the person was told, and what happened when they asked for a human to look again.

articles.asks: The controller is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate, compliance with the principles in Article 5(1).

Inform the person of the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, referred to in Article 22(1) and (4), and at least in those cases give meaningful information about the logic involved and the significance and envisaged consequences.
A person has the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning them or similarly significantly affects them.

That does not apply where the decision is necessary for entering into or performing a contract, is authorised by Union or Member State law with suitable safeguards, or is based on the person's explicit consent.

Where the contract or explicit-consent exception applies, the controller implements suitable measures, at least the right to obtain human intervention, to express one's point of view and to contest the decision.

kinds.title: Automated decision taken
kinds.when: When a decision falling within Article 22(1) is taken, or when you conclude a decision does not fall within it.

fields.name: subject_ref
fields.description: Your pseudonymous reference for the person. Never a name, an email or a national number.

fields.name: solely_automated
fields.description: Whether the decision was based solely on automated processing.

fields.name: significant_effect
fields.description: Whether it produces legal effects concerning the person or similarly significantly affects them.

fields.name: exception
fields.description: The Article 22(2) exception relied on, or that the decision is outside Article 22(1).

fields.name: basis_ref
fields.description: Your reference for the contract, the legal provision or the consent record relied on.

fields.name: information_digest
fields.description: SHA-256 of the notice given to the person about the automated decision, as given.

fields.name: safeguards_offered
fields.description: The safeguards offered with the decision.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: The decision, in a short phrase.

fields.name: decided_at
fields.description: When the decision was taken, UTC.

kinds.title: Human intervention requested and handled
kinds.when: When the person asks for human intervention, expresses a point of view or contests the decision, and again when that request is concluded.

fields.name: subject_ref
fields.description: Your pseudonymous reference for the person. Never a name.

fields.name: decision_record_id
fields.description: The record_id of the gdpr.automated-decision record concerned.

fields.name: reviewer_ref
fields.description: Your reference for the person who reviewed. Never a name.

fields.name: result
fields.description: Where the request stands, or how it ended.

fields.name: reasons
fields.description: Why the decision was upheld, changed or reversed.

example.reasons: Income evidence supplied by the applicant was not available to the model; reassessed manually and approved at a lower limit.

retention: This pack does not state how long to keep these records. The records are yours and hold personal data under your control: keep them no longer than your purposes need, and they stay erasable because they never leave you. Only a salted digest is in the log, and without the record and its salt nobody, including us, can link it to anyone.
notes: Recording that a decision was outside Article 22(1) is as useful as recording one inside it: it shows the question was asked at the time.
